samples.summary: headingLevel is interpolated raw into exported DOCX XML; this change widens which blocks carry the attribute
samples.evidence: `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` builds `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>` with no escaping (docx-style-map.ts:96), while other values in that file go through escapeXml. This change makes `headingLevel` persist on `list-item` blocks in the CRDT tree (memory.ts:258-260, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1413) and restores it into a real `heading` via `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:331-343), so an attacker-controlled attribute on a shared document has one more path back into the exporter. I could not complete an exploit chain: every ingress coerces numerically — `Number(attrs.headingLevel)` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:438 and packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:409, `parseInt` at packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:139,144, and fixed literals from toolbar/clipboard — so a crafted string collapses to NaN, not markup. Hardening only: escape or clamp at the sink so the exporter does not depend on every ingress staying numeric.

samples.summary: No authorization, secret-handling, injection, or crypto surface is touched by this change
samples.evidence: Traced every changed site: the `unlistedBlockType` helper (types.ts), the two keyboard exits in document.ts, the three `toggleList` call sites (editor.ts:2870, text-editor.ts:2169, text-box-editor.ts:1125), and both store implementations. None read credentials, build queries/commands/paths, compare secrets, or gate access. The only new persisted state is a numeric `headingLevel` on `list-item` nodes, which the backend serializer (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:260,408) round-trips as a Number with no validation to bypass, and every reader (docx-exporter.ts:184, pdf-exporter.ts:202, serialize/markdown.ts:103, named-styles.ts:105 with a 1–6 clamp) gates on `type === 'heading'`.
